questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was relevant for my field of study, and I have an interest in future career opportunities in the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I struggled a bit with course selection, but other than that the instructions were clear and I felt nicely welcomed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received very clear instructions about the application process, education, dormatory etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Songle or double rooms at the on-campus dormitory. You can wish for both single and double, but neither is garenteed. (I received confirmation quite early on for my double room)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There are multiple convenience stores close-by, and a cafeteria in the courtyard of the dormitory, as well as others around campus. 
The rooms come with a fridge and freezer and each floor has a kichenette with a hot/cold water, a toaster and a microwave. A big common kitchen was available in another building with a stove and other kitchen remedies.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I found the housing accomoodation more than satisfactory, but if you wish to live privately, there are several private accomodations available as well near campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All instructions were quite clear, and I felt that they got back quickly and clearly upon any inquiries.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a website/platform where everything for the application process is done. You send in applicatoin for exchange, dormitory etc., and get news back about the process on the same webpage.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had very clear instructions on the above-mentioned webpage and were quick to respond over mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite successful. Though I struggled to get the courses I wanted in the first round, most became available upon second application round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be sure to check out the available courses and their given timeslots to have clear priorities ready upon the actual application. 
If possible, do the course registration in Korea as the connection to the server is quite slow from Denmark, and the application process is quite competitive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The education structure wasn't personally the best fit for me due to the strict attendence policy and high expectations for classes with a somewhat low academic level. 
As mentioned the academic level is not as high as in DK, but the expectations for classes are somehow higher. This relating to the attendence, homework, assignments, midterms, exams etc.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both BA and MA courses for my stay. I feel that the MA courses were a better fit, academically for my expectations regarding the quality of education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The graduate course fit better to the teaching style and quality of UCPH. BA courses were very rudementary.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Korean 302. (BA)
2. Introduction to Women's Studies (BA)
3. Thesis Writing (BA)
4. Ceramics 2 (BA)
5. Gender Relations in Contemporary South Korea (MA)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I personally enjoyed all of my courses, but as mentioned the graduate course (Gender Relations in Contemporary South Korea) was incredibly enjoyable with a very skilled and knowledgeble professor. 
Ceramics was also very enjoyable, as you got to work with traditional crafts, while learning about Korea's crafts and history.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Higher commute costs than expected. Also, the obligatory National Health Insurance,

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I have been before, so must followed my expectations. For commuting, I recommend buying the climate card instead of the standard transportation card.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Clubs were mostly unavailable for the fall semester (as it is the 2'nd semester in korea)
They have a good language exchange club where you can meet a local mentor for activities, as well as a buddy group.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See previous answer.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the language exchange and don't be afraid to meet up with other exchange students/locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is plenty to see in Seoul, as well as easily available day-trips to other cities in south korea.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I've lived there before, so I quickly adjusted.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Approach the students in class, and join the buddy group activities. Many feel uncomfortable speaking english, so try to learn a bit Korean and join language exchange.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The education structure was my only struggle. .

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the kindness and welcoming of locals. Especially outside of Seoul.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare for a busy semester, and remember to have fun and go exploring. 
Join as many activities as possible at the beginning of the semester, as you may meet your future friends here. 
Expect extra fees from obligatory NHIS. (health insurance)
Buy climate card for transportation, instead of normal travel card.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sim cards are availbable from chain called chingu mobile woth english speaking staff. They have many locations, often close to the universities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from all over the world, and expliring different cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic structure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
